hypothesis: ml.train owns 58% of the corpus wall clock at an 8.5 s median (evolution/propose.py, 9 p7b traces). RandomForest and XGBoost are constructed with n_jobs=1 and CatBoost at its default thread count, so every training call is single-threaded on a 128-core box. All three are deterministic given random_state for any thread count, so raising the thread count trades cores for wall time and changes no artifact. Measured A/B on p7b_4_drd2: 3.42 s -> 1.89 s (1.81x) with byte-identical metrics (auroc 0.8764, auprc 0.8971, ef@1% 1.705).
risk: More threads per job competes with concurrent jobs for cores; if the executor runs several tickets at once (maxWorkers=3), per-job speedup may not translate into end-to-end throughput. Wall time per step is what this candidate claims, and that is what shadow measures.
